questions.stem: A 65-year-old woman undergoes abdominal CT for vague flank pain. A well-circumscribed, mahogany-brown renal mass with a possible central stellate scar is resected. Pathology shows no necrosis. From which cell type does this tumor originate?
explanations: Incorrect. Proximal tubule cells give rise to clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
Incorrect. Podocytes are visceral epithelial cells of the glomerulus, not the origin of oncocytoma.
Correct. Renal oncocytoma is thought to originate from intercalated cells of the collecting duct.
Incorrect. Perivascular epithelioid cells give rise to angiomyolipoma.
Incorrect. Mesangial cells are glomerular support cells and are unrelated to oncocytoma.

questions.stem: A 70-year-old man undergoes nephrectomy for a renal mass. The resected tumor is mahogany brown, well-circumscribed but not encapsulated, with a central stellate scar and no necrosis. Which diagnosis fits best?
explanations: Incorrect. RCC is golden yellow with hemorrhage and necrosis.
Correct. Mahogany-brown color, sharp circumscription without a capsule, no necrosis, and a central stellate scar are characteristic of renal oncocytoma.
Incorrect. AML contains gross fat and is not described as mahogany brown.
Incorrect. Wilms tumor is a pediatric tumor, not a finding in older adults.
Incorrect. Urothelial carcinoma arises in the urinary tract lining, not as a brown parenchymal mass.

questions.stem: A 68-year-old man with an incidental renal mass undergoes biopsy. Histology shows large cells with small benign-appearing nuclei, no mitotic figures, and intensely eosinophilic cytoplasm. Which organelle accounts for the cytoplasmic appearance?
explanations: Incorrect. Lysosomes do not produce the diffusely eosinophilic appearance described.
Incorrect. Peroxisomes are not the source of cytoplasmic eosinophilia in oncocytoma.
Incorrect. Abundant RER would impart basophilia, not eosinophilia.
Correct. Oncocytes contain abundant mitochondria, giving the cytoplasm its intense eosinophilic appearance.
Incorrect. The Golgi apparatus is not responsible for the eosinophilic cytoplasm of oncocytes.

questions.stem: A 72-year-old man has a 4-cm renal mass detected incidentally on CT. He has no symptoms. According to the brick, what fraction of patients with renal oncocytoma are asymptomatic?
explanations: Incorrect. Only a minority of patients have symptoms; the asymptomatic fraction is higher.
Incorrect. The brick specifies a higher proportion than half.
Correct. About three-quarters (75%) of patients with renal oncocytoma are asymptomatic.
Incorrect. A small fraction do have symptoms such as hematuria or flank pain.
Incorrect. Some patients are symptomatic, so the asymptomatic fraction is not 100%.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man with a renal oncocytoma develops gross hematuria, flank pain, and a palpable flank mass. This triad is most classically associated with which malignancy that oncocytoma can mimic?
explanations: Incorrect. Wilms tumor is a pediatric tumor and does not share this adult triad.
Incorrect. Bladder SCC presents with terminal hematuria, not a flank mass triad.
Correct. The triad of hematuria, flank pain, and flank mass is classically described for renal cell carcinoma, and oncocytoma can mimic it.
Incorrect. Urothelial carcinoma typically presents with painless hematuria, not this triad.
Incorrect. Adrenal cortical carcinoma is not the tumor associated with this triad.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man undergoes resection of a renal mass. Gross examination reveals invasion into the renal vein and perirenal fat. Which feature does this finding argue against?
explanations: Correct. Renal oncocytomas never grossly invade renal vessels or perirenal fat; such invasion essentially excludes oncocytoma and favors RCC.
Incorrect. Clear cell RCC commonly invades the renal vein.
Incorrect. Papillary RCC can invade vessels and perirenal fat.
Incorrect. Sarcomatoid RCC is aggressive and can show vascular invasion.
Incorrect. Collecting duct carcinoma is malignant and can invade adjacent structures.

questions.stem: A 66-year-old man undergoes CT for hematuria. A small, sharply demarcated renal lesion with a central stellate scar is seen. Why does the brick still recommend surgical resection despite the suggestive imaging?
explanations: Incorrect. A central stellate scar is characteristic of oncocytoma but is also seen in RCC.
Correct. Imaging cannot reliably distinguish oncocytoma from RCC, so resection is performed to exclude malignancy.
Incorrect. Oncocytomas are benign and do not metastasize.
Incorrect. Radiotherapy is not the management strategy described in the brick.
Incorrect. Tuberous sclerosis is associated with angiomyolipoma, not oncocytoma.

questions.stem: A 71-year-old patient is diagnosed with a 3-cm renal oncocytoma. According to the brick, which management is most appropriate?
explanations: Correct. Surgical resection is the most common treatment because oncocytoma cannot reliably be distinguished from RCC preoperatively.
Incorrect. Watchful waiting alone is not the standard because malignancy cannot be excluded by imaging.
Incorrect. Radiation therapy is not the standard treatment for oncocytoma.
Incorrect. IL-2 immunotherapy is used for metastatic RCC, not benign oncocytoma.
Incorrect. Antibiotics have no role in treating a renal tumor.

questions.stem: A 64-year-old man with a small renal oncocytoma wishes to preserve as much functional kidney tissue as possible. Which surgical option does the brick describe for this purpose?
explanations: Incorrect. Radical nephrectomy removes the entire kidney and sacrifices normal tissue.
Incorrect. Bilateral nephrectomy would leave the patient anephric.
Correct. Partial nephrectomy can be used to preserve normal kidney tissue when resecting an oncocytoma.
Incorrect. Ureteral stenting addresses obstruction, not parenchymal tumors.
Incorrect. Adrenalectomy targets the adrenal gland, not the kidney.

questions.stem: A 78-year-old man with multiple comorbidities is found to have a small renal oncocytoma. He is a poor surgical candidate. Which non-surgical option does the brick list as an alternative?
explanations: Incorrect. Plasma exchange is not used for solid renal tumors.
Incorrect. Cisplatin chemoembolization is not the brick's described alternative.
Incorrect. External beam radiation is not described as standard therapy.
Correct. Cryoablation and radiofrequency ablation are described as alternatives to surgical resection.
Incorrect. Hemodialysis treats renal failure, not renal tumors.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old woman is found to have a renal mass composed grossly of fat, smooth muscle, and abnormal blood vessels. Which tumor is this?
explanations: Incorrect. Oncocytomas are composed of eosinophilic oncocytes, not fat and smooth muscle.
Incorrect. Wilms tumor contains blastemal, stromal, and epithelial elements, not classical AML components.
Correct. Angiomyolipoma is composed of blood vessels (angio), smooth muscle (myo), and fat (lipo).
Incorrect. Clear cell RCC consists of polygonal clear cells, not the three AML components.
Incorrect. Urothelial carcinoma arises from urothelium and does not contain fat and smooth muscle.

questions.stem: A 14-year-old boy with hypopigmented skin macules, facial angiofibromas, and epilepsy is found on imaging to have multiple bilateral renal masses with gross fat. Which underlying genetic syndrome is most likely?
explanations: Incorrect. VHL is associated with clear cell RCC and hemangioblastomas, not AML.
Incorrect. NF1 features neurofibromas and cafe-au-lait spots, not AML.
Incorrect. NF2 causes bilateral vestibular schwannomas, not AML.
Incorrect. Sturge-Weber features port-wine stains and leptomeningeal angiomas, not AML.
Correct. Tuberous sclerosis features angiofibromas, hypopigmented macules, epilepsy, and renal AMLs.

questions.stem: A 22-year-old woman with tuberous sclerosis has multiple bilateral renal angiomyolipomas. Loss-of-function mutations in which gene pair underlie her tumors?
explanations: Incorrect. VHL mutations cause Von Hippel-Lindau syndrome, not tuberous sclerosis.
Correct. AML in tuberous sclerosis is caused by loss-of-function mutations in the TSC1 and TSC2 tumor suppressor genes.
Incorrect. BRCA mutations predispose to breast and ovarian cancers.
Incorrect. MLH1 and MSH2 are mismatch repair genes in Lynch syndrome.
Incorrect. RB1 and TP53 are tumor suppressors not specifically tied to AML.

questions.stem: A 50-year-old woman has a sporadic renal angiomyolipoma found incidentally. According to the brick, which demographic pattern fits sporadic AML?
explanations: Incorrect. Sporadic AML is a tumor of adults, not children.
Correct. Sporadic AML usually occurs in adults over 40-50 with a female-to-male ratio of about 4:1.
Incorrect. The brick describes a female, not male, predominance for sporadic AML.
Incorrect. Young patients with no sex predilection describes TSC-associated AML.
Incorrect. The age range described is over 40-50, not strictly elderly.

questions.stem: A 35-year-old woman with a 7-cm renal angiomyolipoma presents with sudden severe flank pain, gross hematuria, hypotension, and a drop in hemoglobin. Which complication is most likely?
explanations: Incorrect. Pyelonephritis presents with fever and pyuria, not hemorrhagic shock.
Incorrect. Renal vein thrombosis does not typically cause hemorrhagic shock from AML.
Correct. Dilated abnormal vessels in AML can rupture, producing retroperitoneal hemorrhage with hypotension and anemia.
Incorrect. ATN is a tubular injury, not a hemorrhagic complication of AML.
Incorrect. Malignant transformation is rare and does not cause this acute presentation.

questions.stem: A 40-year-old woman with a known angiomyolipoma is admitted with hemorrhagic shock. The brick notes the retroperitoneal space can occultly hold up to what volume of blood?
explanations: Incorrect. The retroperitoneum can accommodate far more than 500 mL.
Incorrect. 1 L is below the threshold described in the brick.
Incorrect. The brick specifies a larger volume than 2 L.
Correct. The retroperitoneal space can hold up to 4 L of blood without becoming externally visible.
Incorrect. 10 L exceeds the brick's stated capacity.

questions.stem: A 38-year-old woman undergoes resection of a renal AML. Histology shows thick-walled vessels, spindle-shaped smooth muscle cells, and adipose tissue. Which AML variant is this?
explanations: Incorrect. The epithelioid variant contains large eosinophilic epithelial-like cells.
Correct. The classic AML variant contains thick-walled vessels, spindle-shaped smooth muscle cells, and adipose tissue.
Incorrect. Papillary architecture is a feature of papillary RCC, not classic AML.
Incorrect. Sarcomatoid features describe aggressive RCC, not classic AML.
Incorrect. A cystic variant is not the histology described.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old man with renal AML undergoes resection. Histology shows large epithelial-like eosinophilic cells. Which complication is most associated with this AML variant?
explanations: Incorrect. Spontaneous regression is not the described concern.
Incorrect. Calcification is not the typical concern; AMLs are usually identified by fat, not calcium.
Incorrect. AML does not convert to oncocytoma.
Correct. The epithelioid variant of AML may transform into a malignant tumor with distant metastases.
Incorrect. Fistula formation to bowel is not the brick's described complication.

questions.stem: A 48-year-old woman has a renal mass discovered on imaging. Which imaging feature on CT scan helps distinguish angiomyolipoma from renal cell carcinoma?
explanations: Incorrect. A central stellate scar is characteristic of oncocytoma, not AML.
Correct. Macroscopic fat without calcifications on CT helps distinguish AML from RCC; fat appears as a darker density area.
Incorrect. Golden yellow color is a gross pathologic finding of RCC, not an imaging finding.
Incorrect. Cortical thinning is nonspecific and does not distinguish AML from RCC.
Incorrect. Calcifications are typical of RCC and argue against AML.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man has a suspected renal AML. According to the brick, which two imaging modalities are preferred for diagnosis?
explanations: Correct. Computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging are the two preferred imaging modalities for diagnosing AML.
Incorrect. Plain films and fluoroscopy do not characterize renal masses adequately.
Incorrect. PET-CT and bone scan are not the preferred modalities for AML.
Incorrect. Mammography and DEXA evaluate breasts and bone density, not the kidney.
Incorrect. Scintigraphy and arteriography are not the brick's preferred modalities.

questions.stem: A 42-year-old woman has an asymptomatic 35-mm renal AML found on CT. According to the brick, what is the most appropriate management?
explanations: Incorrect. Asymptomatic small AMLs do not require immediate nephrectomy.
Incorrect. Embolization is reserved for large or symptomatic lesions.
Incorrect. AML is benign in most cases and chemotherapy is not indicated.
Correct. Asymptomatic small AMLs are managed with surveillance imaging.
Incorrect. Transplant evaluation is unrelated to small asymptomatic AML.

questions.stem: A 50-year-old man has a 7-cm symptomatic renal AML with recurrent flank pain. Which two interventional options does the brick list for large or symptomatic tumors?
explanations: Incorrect. Steroids are not indicated for AML; large symptomatic tumors require intervention.
Correct. Large (>60 mm) or symptomatic AMLs can be embolized via intravascular catheter or resected with partial nephrectomy.
Incorrect. Radiation and IL-2 are not the brick's listed interventions for AML.
Incorrect. Plasmapheresis and dialysis do not treat AML.
Incorrect. Antibiotics and NSAIDs do not address the tumor itself.

questions.stem: A 25-year-old woman with tuberous sclerosis has multiple rapidly growing bilateral AMLs. Which medication targets the underlying pathway and can shrink these tumors while preserving renal function?
explanations: Incorrect. Cyclosporine is a calcineurin inhibitor used for immunosuppression, not AML shrinkage.
Correct. Everolimus is an mTOR inhibitor that can reduce AML size and preserve renal function in TSC-associated disease.
Incorrect. Tacrolimus is a calcineurin inhibitor, not an mTOR inhibitor.
Incorrect. Hydroxyurea is used for sickle cell disease and myeloproliferative disorders.
Incorrect. Methotrexate is an antimetabolite, not an mTOR inhibitor.

questions.stem: A medical student is reading about everolimus for tuberous sclerosis-associated AML. The drug inhibits a serine/threonine kinase regulating cell growth and metabolism. What is this target?
explanations: Correct. mTOR (mammalian target of rapamycin) is a serine/threonine kinase that regulates cell growth and metabolism; everolimus inhibits it.
Incorrect. JAK2 is targeted by ruxolitinib in myeloproliferative neoplasms.
Incorrect. BRAF is targeted by vemurafenib in melanoma.
Incorrect. EGFR is targeted by drugs like erlotinib for lung cancer.
Incorrect. VEGF receptors are targeted by drugs like sunitinib, not everolimus.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man with acute cholecystitis has an incidental small left kidney lesion found on abdominal ultrasound. He has no urinary symptoms and no history of tuberous sclerosis. On follow-up CT, which feature would most strongly favor angiomyolipoma over oncocytoma?
explanations: Incorrect. Mahogany-brown color is a gross pathologic feature of oncocytoma.
Incorrect. A central stellate scar suggests oncocytoma (or RCC), not AML.
Incorrect. Hemorrhage and necrosis favor RCC over either oncocytoma or AML.
Correct. Macroscopic fat on CT is the helpful radiographic feature pointing toward AML.
Incorrect. Renal vein invasion strongly suggests RCC, not AML or oncocytoma.
